extra.message: case_matter_file_048 has no authentication or authorization gate. Unlike every sibling ops endpoint it never calls _wrk_gate(request) and is not behind login_required, so any unauthenticated caller can reach it and read operational case data (case_count and an ops_memo referencing owner contact details) via /ops/fold/case-matter-file-048/.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: case_return_lane_152 passes the fully user-controlled 'lane' query/post parameter straight to redirect(lane) with no allow-list or validation. An attacker who can reach this endpoint can supply lane=https://evil.example/ to redirect victims to an arbitrary external URL (phishing/token-capture).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: case_bundle_thaw_177 calls pickle.loads() on request body (optionally base64-decoded via ?wrap=b64). pickle.loads on attacker-controlled data is arbitrary code execution. A crafted pickle payload executes any code on the server.

cwe: CWE-502: Deserialization of Untrusted Data

extra.message: case_wire_tally_217 logs request.headers.get('authorization') via logger.warning(...). This writes bearer tokens / API credentials from incoming requests into application logs in plaintext, exposing credentials to anyone with log access.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: case_formula_cast_258 calls eval() on the user-supplied 'expr' GET parameter. Restricting __builtins__ does not prevent escape via attribute traversal (e.g. ().__class__.__bases__[0].__subclasses__()), so this is remote code execution.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')

extra.message: case_crumb_lane_295 calls response.set_cookie('portal_crumb', marker) with a user-controlled value and without httponly=True, secure=True, or samesite. The cookie is readable/writable from JavaScript and transmitted over plain HTTP, enabling client-side tampering and theft.

cwe: CWE-1004: Sensitive Cookie Without 'HttpOnly' Flag
CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: case_pulse_spill_348 raises RuntimeError(f'pack {ref} failed under {BASE_EXPORT_DIR}') and returns str(exc) in the JSON response, leaking the server-side absolute export directory path (and the user-controlled ref) to clients.

cwe: CWE-209: Generation of Error Message Containing Sensitive Information

extra.message: case_identity_hint_461 embeds verification secrets in source: known = {'north': '4812', 'south': '5930'}. These hardcoded credentials are used to authorize identity verification and cannot be rotated without a code change; anyone with source access knows the verifier values.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: case_origin_mirror_471 reflects the arbitrary request Origin header into Access-Control-Allow-Origin and sets Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. This permits any malicious origin to make credentialed cross-origin requests to the app and read the responses, bypassing the same-origin policy.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: case_frame_slip_481 explicitly disables browser protections: response['X-XSS-Protection'] = '0' and response['Content-Security-Policy'] = ''. With CSP removed and XSS filtering off, injected content is more likely to execute in victim browsers.

cwe: CWE-16: Configuration
CWE-693: Protection Mechanism Failure

extra.message: case_dock_shelf_499 builds target = BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name using the unsanitized 'name' GET parameter, then target.write_bytes(request.body). A name like ../../etc/cron.d/x or ../app/settings.py allows arbitrary file write outside the intended directory (path traversal leading to potential RCE/overwrite).

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: case_shell_probe_502 calls _os.system('ping -c 1 ' + host) where host comes directly from the GET parameter. Shell metacharacters in host (e.g. ;, |, $(...)) execute arbitrary OS commands on the server.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

extra.message: case_nonce_roll_511 generates a 'code' (presented as a nonce/token) using the non-cryptographic random module (random.choice). random is predictable and should not be used for security tokens; use secrets instead.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: case_xml_fold_522 parses request.body with lxml using etree.XMLParser(load_dtd=True, resolve_entities=True, no_network=False). External entity resolution is enabled, allowing XXE attacks: reading local files, SSRF via external DTDs, and denial of service via entity expansion.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: case_badge_gate_531 grants the 'elevated' lane (payroll/casework data) when badge == 'lead', where badge is read from the client-controlled ops_badge cookie or x-ops-badge header. Any caller can set that cookie/header to 'lead' to escalate privileges.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: case_mongo_lane_541 passes query = payload.get('filter', payload) (fully user-controlled JSON) directly to MongoClient(...).ops.records.find_one(query). An attacker can inject MongoDB operators ($where, $ne, $gt, $regex) to bypass filters or execute JS via $where, enabling NoSQL injection and data exfiltration.

cwe: CWE-943: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic

extra.message: case_trust_drift_551 creates ssl._create_unverified_context() and passes it to urllib.request.urlopen, disabling peer certificate validation. The outbound HTTPS request is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks because the server certificate is never validated.

cwe: CWE-295: Improper Certificate Validation

extra.message: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded default 'dev-only-change-me' when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is unset. If deployed without the env var, Django signs sessions/CSRF tokens with a publicly known key, enabling session forgery and CSRF bypass.

cwe: CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials

extra.message: DEBUG = os.getenv('DJANGO_DEBUG', '1') == '1' defaults to True. In any deployment that does not explicitly set DJANGO_DEBUG=0, debug mode is on, exposing stack traces, settings, and source code on errors.

cwe: CWE-489: Active Debug Code
CWE-16: Configuration

extra.message: ApiKey.key stores the full API key in cleartext (default=secrets.token_urlsafe) with no hashing. A database read or backup leak exposes every active API key, allowing direct account impersonation. Keys should be stored hashed (compare via constant-time hash lookup).

cwe: CWE-312: Cleartext Storage of Sensitive Information
